name: veterinary_clinic_system_096_temporal_anomaly_detection
instruction: Temporal data quality sweep — mutate nothing. Find all temporal impossibilities and near-impossibilities across the seed data and produce one ops_reports row {report: 'temporal_anomalies', batch_code, anomalies: <total>, by_rule: {<rule_name>: <count>}, row_refs: {<rule_name>: [<ascending ids>]}, clean: <true iff total == 0>}. The sweep must include these rules (derive from the data and clinical record-keeping norms; include zero-count rules; do not modify any collection): (a) appointment time inversion: an appointment's end_time is not strictly after its start_time; (b) vaccine due before administration: a vaccination's due_date is strictly before its administered_date; (c) visit record locked too early: a visit record's locked_at exists and is fewer than 30 days after its visit_date; (d) lab result before visit: a lab_result's resulted_at is strictly before the latest visit_records.visit_date for the same patient; (e) reminder queued after due: a reminder_queue row with a due_date has due_date strictly before queued_at; (f) estimate expires before created: a billing_estimates expires_date is strictly before its created_at. Row refs must be sorted within each rule and empty for clean rules.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: Canary every collection except ops_reports. Recompute the six rule counts and row-id lists two independent ways (Python over fetch_all and SQL SELECT/COUNT). Assert the ops_reports row matches exactly, including empty lists for clean rules.

checks.expect: each rule count/row set is computed via both Python and SQL
exactly one temporal_anomalies row with matching by_rule/row_refs/anomalies/clean

hazards: appointment time inversion: 274 appointments have end_time <= start_time (e.g., id 7 start_time 12:30, end_time 12:00; id 9 start 15:30, end 15:00). The seed reverses start/end for exactly half the appointment rows.

vaccine due before administration: 10 vaccinations have due_date < administered_date (e.g., id 100 FVRCP patient 50 administered 2026-08-19, due 2026-07-23; id 134 bordetella patient 67 administered 2026-07-15, due 2026-06-27).
visit record locked too early: 344 visit_records have a locked_at fewer than 30 days after visit_date (e.g., id 1 visit_date 2026-01-05, locked_at 2026-01-06).
lab result before latest visit: 11 lab_results have resulted_at before the patient's latest visit_date (ids 8,12,13,14,23,25,26,28,32,38,39).
reminder due before queued: exactly reminder_queue id 1 has due_date 2026-08-14 and queued_at 2026-09-03. Reminder id 2 (due 2026-09-10) and id 4 (no due_date) are not violations.

estimate expires before created: 0 rows, because every billing_estimates.expires_date is after its created_at. This is a zero-count rule that a lazy solution must still include as an empty row_ref list.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: A multi-collection temporal-impossibility sweep with cross-collection rules (lab vs visit, reminder due vs queued, visit lock vs 30-day rule) and dual-path verification. The large but real counts (274 time inversions, 344 early locks) make brute-force inspection infeasible and force programmatic filtering.
